newsitem.title: GERMANY: TAKEOVER TALK BOOSTS COMMERZBANK SHARES.
newsitem.headline: TAKEOVER TALK BOOSTS COMMERZBANK SHARES.

text.p: A fresh wave of takeover speculation fuelled interest in Commerzbank AG shares on Friday, sending the bank's stock soaring in a downward trending market.
Commerzbank was leading turnover volumes and trading up 1.90 marks, or three percent, at 65.35 marks at 0925 GMT.
Germany's 30-share DAX index was down 0.7 percent at 4,384.10 points.

Dealers said a whole range of speculation was sweeping through the market, a follow-on from an almost unbroken year of merger rumours in the German banking sector, which is viewed as overcrowded and ripe for consolidation.
There was talk that Commerzbank would be taken over by Deutsche Bank AG or by HSBC Bank, dealers said, while cautioning that they did not give much credence to the talk.
The German banking sector has been hit by a new wave of consolidation rumours since last month's news of plans for a major merger in Bavaria, creating Germany's second largest commercial bank.
Commerzbank has steadfastly said it is not a takeover candidate and would be too expensive for any potential buyer.
